purpose: Read-only local snapshot of the project's derived global rules. Nothing here is ever written back to the project.

rules.rule: Return four candidate options from four different template IDs for every shot.
Include at least one infographic candidate whenever infographics are allowed for the shot.
Score the presentation template independently from the identity and relevance of the replacement assets; a good template with the wrong artist assets is not a successful plan.
Choose the visual focal subject from the passage’s main claim, not merely the first named entity. Open on the primary subject when a supporting example is named first.
When one passage names an artifact, a catalog, projects, or proof, request every supporting visual needed to establish those clauses rather than returning one generic portrait.
For gap, distance, overlap, outlier, or falling-rank claims, retrieve spatial/3D candidates before ordinary comparison charts.
Rules, lists, and evidence text require a calm readable hold; reject scenes whose motion or layout prevents reading.
Split a passage when data visualization, portrait footage, documentary evidence, or qualitative comparison require different visual treatments.
When footage directly shows the named people, event, performance, or claim, include it as a candidate instead of considering only still images.
A setup visual may intentionally hold into the following reveal and then populate with data rather than cutting to an unrelated template.
